chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Kufi, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Salih al-Razi, from Hamman al-Dibani, who said: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:

Whoever visits me from a distance of my dwelling, I will come to him on the Day of Resurrection in three occasions until I liberate him from its terrors: When the Books [of Deeds] are spread out to the right and left, At the Bridge [al-Sirat], and At the Scale [al-Mizan].
ai.seo_question: How does visiting the Imam's shrine benefit the pilgrim on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith to highlight the intercessory role of the Imams, specifically Imam al-Rida (as), in mitigating the fears of the Hereafter for their devotees. This promise of personal assistance during the distribution of the Books, crossing the Sirat, and the weighing of deeds underscores the Shia belief in the spiritual proximity of the Ahl al-Bayt to the believers. It serves as a theological assurance that righteous visitation (Ziyarah) yields tangible eschatological benefits beyond mere ritual observance.
